items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: I'll have to later anyway, get a new amplifier. And I'll copy that if I don't get it done before, which Mrs. Rankin has asked about, a George Bakke and a Sidney Bechet duet that John Reed had recorded.

ctx.x: Yeah. For some reason, they called them bootleggers. It means that they were pirated. One of the labels is called Jolly Roger. And incidentally, Victor would press those things for those guys. They'd steal the Victor rights, you might say. They didn't steal anything directly because it wasn't the actual property. But they'd take the records off, copy them, and issue them on another record. And Victor was pressing their own material for other people, which they always refused to do if they knew it. But they never…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: I'll send some of these and go over the ones that you don't, that I don't have here, like George Bakke and Johnny Dodds notes.

ctx.x: I have a record he made with Joe Dierensburg. He might have played a little bit after that, not much.

So, because he, I heard. The LARP record? Yeah. It was made about that time, actually. He had cancer, I heard, at that time. He looked in pretty good health and talked like he'd be playing, like he was alright. But a couple years later, maybe about two years ago, he died. So, evidently he did have cancer. And he was one of the better drummers, not flashy in any way either. And maybe in some sense, monotonous compared to some of the other New Orleans drummers, but still a wonderful rhythm section.
